description: Official FP Sudoku-hard checkpoint, measurement only. A: body (32 layers) perturbed by INT8/4/3, ternary, or Gaussian noise with matched per-layer relative Frobenius error (first 500 test puzzles). B: ternary (absmean per-tensor) applied to single layers / blocks / first-k / last-k blocks (first 256 test puzzles). Notebook ncm_asama2b_qat.ipynb section 11, module colab/ncm_diag.py.

theory.note: Computed numerically on 4M N(0,1) samples (TWN-style threshold search, L2-optimal scale).

conclusions: Collapse is governed by error magnitude, not by ternary per se: Gaussian noise with the same relative error degrades the model like quantization does (int4 0.19 -> 83.4 vs noise 0.20 -> 80.8; int3 0.42 and noise 0.40 both 0).

Tolerance threshold: 50% solve rate at rel_err ~0.28; >=0.35 gives ~0. Even optimal ternary has rel_err >= ~0.44 for Gaussian weights (measured 0.47-0.56 on real weights), so any per-layer ternary PTQ must fail on this model.

Error does not cascade across levels: with ternary weights TF accuracy (true previous codes given) is already ~0.1 at every level, close to generation accuracy; 446/500 puzzles diverge from FP already at level 0. The damage is in the transformer's per-level prediction, accumulating with depth (hidden-state drift 0.37 after block 0 -> 1.01 after block 7).

Sensitivity is concentrated at the input: wte alone, or block-0 attention alone, gives 0%. The earlier 'io_only (0.9% of params) -> 0%' result is caused by the input projection wte, not by the 12 output heads (each head ternarized alone: ~85%).
Generation codes are not unique: INT8 keeps 84.8% solved but only 41.8% identical codes; noise 0.05 keeps 85.8% with 1.6% identical codes.
note: Transcribed from pasted Colab log. Deterministic (noise seed 0). Subsets of the test set.
